item.title: Quantum Natural Muon: Spectral-Natural Optimization for Variational Quantum Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2611.10105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training parameterized quantum circuits requires optimization methods that account for two distinct structures: the information geometry of quantum states and the matrix or tensor structure induced by circuit parameterization. We introduce Quantum Natural Muon (QNM), a spectral natural-gradient framework that applies polar normalization to circuit-semantic parameter blocks after damped quantum Fisher preconditioning. This ordering is essential: quantum Fisher preconditioning and blockwise polar normalization do not commute in general, so QNM is not an order-free composition of quantum natural gradient (QNG) and Muon. We show that Frobenius-matched polar mixing preserves active singular subspaces while raising a spectral floor and improving active conditioning, and that the resulting direction remains a controlled perturbation of QNG. For its distance-aware realization (DA-QNM), we further establish alignment, descent, and nonconvex stationarity guarantees for the normalized update, together with perturbation bounds under gradient and QFIM estimation error. Experiments on variational quantum eigensolving, weighted QAOA-MaxCut, and supervised quantum classification isolate the roles of quantum geometry, circuit-semantic spectral structure, and radius control. The strongest gains arise when the spectral blocks match the circuit structure, supporting the central principle that quantum-state and structured spectral geometries provide complementary information for variational quantum optimization.
item.dc:creator: Duong The Do, Duong Tung Nguyen

item.title: Open-Source Multi-Fidelity EMT Modeling of Data Center Loads for Power System Studies
item.description: arXiv:2611.10179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Characterizing data center-grid interactions under rapid load fluctuations requires electromagnetic transient (EMT) models that capture fast converter and control dynamics. This paper develops a modular multi-fidelity EMT model of data center loads in PSCAD. The modular design supports flexible assembly of subsystem models for different power supply configurations. The multi-fidelity design incorporates switching models, average-converter models, and reduced-order models to balance simulation accuracy and computational efficiency according to analysis needs. The model also provides a systematic controller tuning procedure and supports control mode switching. Comparative simulations demonstrate how this data center load model responds to both grid-side and load-side disturbances and assess the accuracy and computational efficiency of models with three fidelity levels. The model is publicly available on GitHub.
item.dc:creator: Xingyu Zhao, Yingyi Tang, Junbo Zhao

item.title: Control of Linear Dynamical Systems with Operational Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.10214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a method for designing servo-controllers that enforce operational constraints on multi-input multi-output linear time-invariant dynamical systems. The proposed method introduces a control augmentation that complements a baseline controller to ensure forward invariance of state/output trajectories within prescribed box constraints. The derivations of the control design are based on the Nagumo Theorem, the Comparison Lemma, and principles from min-norm optimal control akin to the theory of Control Barrier Functions. Importantly, an explicit piecewise-linear feedback control law is derived, which provides continuous enforcement of constraints without online optimization, enabling rigorous stability and robustness analysis via classical linear systems theory. Extensions to handle estimation errors in output feedback and integral action in proportional-integral control are provided. Theoretical results are validated through flight control simulation studies that demonstrate input/output constraint satisfaction, robustness to disturbances, and closed-loop stability. The proposed method offers a mathematically rigorous, practical, and analyzable alternative to common heuristic or optimization-intensive constrained control strategies.
item.dc:creator: Marcel Menner, Eugene Lavretsky

item.title: Sample-Covariance Regularization for Data-Driven Predictive Control from Frequency Response Functions under Colored Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.10226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate how sample covariance obtained from frequency-response functions (FRFs) can be exploited to improve performance of data-driven frequency-domain predictive control (FreePC) in the presence of colored measurement noise. In case of periodic multisine excitation, this covariance is obtained directly from repeated periods and provides a frequency-dependent measure of uncertainty without requiring an additional parametric noise model. To incorporate this information into both indirect and direct predictive control, we develop a frequency-domain subspace predictive controller (FD-SPC) and establish its equivalence to the direct FreePC formulation in the noiseless setting. Regularization terms for both formulations are then motivated by expected prediction-error criteria and constructed from the sample covariance of the FRF estimates. Across all tested noise models and data sizes, regularization consistently reduces the median realized control cost relative to the corresponding controller without covariance regularization, with reductions of up to 35%.
item.dc:creator: M. Wind, T. J. Meijer, V. S. Dolk, W. P. M. H. Heemels

item.title: Dynamic Traffic Modeling using Equivalent Circuit Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.10246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an equivalent circuit model (ECM) for dynamic traffic modeling by exploiting analogies between electrical and transportation variables. Vehicle concentration is represented by capacitor voltage, while traffic flow is modeled using controllable current sources. The proposed formulation is shown to preserve the conservation and sending/receiving relationships of the spatially discretized Lighthill Whitham Richards traffic model. The framework is extended to restricted inflow, traffic signals, and two road merging and diverging scenarios. Validation against microscopic Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) simulations, involving traffic signals, two-road merging, and single-road diverging scenarios, demonstrates that the proposed ECM successfully reproduces the principal macroscopic traffic dynamics, including queue formation, backward congestion propagation, vehicle accumulation, saturation, and subsequent traffic recovery.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Moyalan, Ricardo de Castro, Iman Ebrahimi, Xuchang Tang, Xinfan Lin

item.title: Simulating Nonlinear Resistive Networks using a Behavioral Splitting
item.description: arXiv:2611.10361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An operator splitting method is developed for computing operating points of nonlinear resistive networks. Our behavioral formulation separates the device laws from Kirchhoff's laws and casts simulation as a zero-finding problem. Branch port resistances then provide a diagonal preconditioner for the relaxed Peaceman-Rachford iteration in scattering variables. Each iteration requires solving independent scalar equations and a linear system with a fixed weighted Laplacian matrix. Convergence is established for maximal monotone device laws when an operating point exists. Contractive branch reflections also yield a linear convergence bound independent of network topology. Numerical experiments on crossbar arrays illustrate the computational advantages.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alizadeh, Thomas Chaffey, Dominic Liao-McPherson, Alberto Padoan

item.title: On Real Eventual Exponential Positive property of complex-valued Laplacians and their pseudoinverses
item.description: arXiv:2611.10496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The property of real eventual exponential positivity guarantees the state trajectories of a linear time-invariant system to evolve asymptotically to right half of the complex-plane [1]. It has applications in the characterization of herdability and reachability of states in networked systems. Networks with complex-valued edge-weights arise in AC power systems and opinion dynamics. Recent work has introduced real eventual exponential positive (rEEP) Laplacians, for which the trajectories of the associated network flow eventually converge to consensus. We establish further properties of rEEP Laplacians and their pseudoinverses. Firstly, we show that the rEEP property for complex-valued matrices exhibits invariance under specific rotational transformations. Secondly, we establish that the property of rEEP is preserved under the MoorePenrose pseudoinverse operation, highlighting its robustness under algebraic manipulations. These results apply to effective impedance computation in AC networks and to consensus in multi-agent systems. Finally, we provide numerical examples to validate our theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Aditi Saxena, Twinkle Tripathy, Rajasekhar Anguluri

item.title: Balancing Confidentiality and Attack Detectability in Networked Control Systems over Lossy Wireless Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.10554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the joint protection of a networked control system (NCS) against eavesdropping and data integrity attacks over a lossy wireless channel. The eavesdropper intercepts the transmitted sensor measurements and control inputs to reconstruct the system state. In contrast, the integrity attacker in this study replaces the sensor measurements with fabricated data to drive the system to undesired operating conditions. Although these two threats are typically studied separately, a wireless NCS should be protected against both simultaneously, and a defence against one affects the other. We employ an observation-encoding scheme that renders the eavesdropper's state-estimation error covariance unbounded under packet drops, and show that transmission energy governs how long this error remains bounded. In particular, lower transmission energy improves confidentiality. For integrity protection, we combine stochastic physical watermarking with a CUSUM-based sequential change detector. The proposed attack detection scheme accounts for intermittent communication and encoded measurements. The detection delay is governed by the Kullback--Leibler divergence (KLD) between the pre- and post-attack distributions of the test signal, and we show that a higher transmission energy increases the KLD and thereby reduces the detection delay. Furthermore, we derive analytical expressions for the eavesdropper's estimation error and the worst-case expected KLD, providing guidelines for selecting transmission energy to balance confidentiality and integrity protection and characterising the privacy--security trade-off. Finally, we run numerical simulations to validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the privacy--security trade-off in practical scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Mahyar Mohammadi, Subhrakanti Dey, Arunava Naha

item.title: Shifted Interaction Functions: A Unified Framework for Imperfect Actuation and Sensing in Consensus Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.10582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Practical networked robotic systems rarely implement ideal consensus interactions exactly, since local actuation constraints, sensing biases, and heterogeneous interaction maps may shift the input-output relations used by distributed controllers. Rather than focusing solely on whether consensus occurs, such imperfections can fundamentally alter the structure of the asymptotic collective behavior, typically yielding global or clustered velocity alignment, while exact static agreement arises only in special cases. This paper develops a shifted-interaction framework for analyzing collective alignment under imperfect actuation and sensing. Shifted functions provide a compact representation of local actuator and sensor maps, allowing actuation constraints and sensing biases to be represented by horizontally and vertically shifted monotone interactions. The framework distinguishes nodal shifted actuation from edge-wise shifted sensing. For shifted actuation, a Lyapunov analysis establishes global velocity alignment under compatible actuation ranges, including bounded, non-invertible, and deadzone-type maps. For shifted sensing, a maximum-principle argument and a paired-sensitivity condition establish convergence to velocity clusters over edges with infinite accumulated sensitivity; uniform sensing sensitivity yields exponential global velocity alignment. In the linear case, closed-form expressions characterize asymptotic behavior and identify actuation as a special case of sensing. Simulations illustrate static, globally aligned, and clustered velocity-aligned behaviors.
item.dc:creator: Yang Xu, Enric Morella Violeta, Hector Garcia de Marina

item.title: Two-Timescale Trajectory Control, Task Reassignment and Resource Scheduling for Multi-UAV Cooperative Mobile Edge Computing
item.description: arXiv:2611.10673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) is a promising technology, leveraging the advantages of UAVs including flexible deployment, wide coverage, and reliable wireless communication. In this paper, we study the task reassignment and offloading problem in a multi-UAV cooperative operating environment, and consider the real occurrence that the computing tasks arrive more frequently than UAVs make flight decisions. In addition, we also take into account the position offset of the UAV during flight and the unavailability of the UAV due to external interference. We propose a two-timescale optimization framework, where the trajectory of the UAV is carried out on a large timescale, while the task reassignment and computing resource allocation are jointly optimized on a small timescale. The core objective is to maximize the long-term average system gain, which takes both energy consumption and task delay into account. To address the UAV trajectory optimization problem under large timescale constraints, we propose a constrained multi-agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm. For decision-making within small timescale, to jointly optimize task offloading decisions and computing resource allocation, we integrate convex optimization with a heuristic algorithm. Finally, we conduct extensive simulations to evaluate the proposed algorithms against the baseline, achieving a 24% reduction in latency and a 28% reduction in total system cost.
item.dc:creator: Bin Li, Shiyu Sun, Lei Liu, Zesong Fei

item.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Massively Parallel Simulation for Low-Thrust Multi-Revolution Rendezvous
item.description: arXiv:2611.10712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing demand for on-orbit servicing and constellation management in low Earth orbit requires autonomous and reliable low-thrust rendezvous. Traditional numerical methods struggle with the long-horizon nature of multi-revolution maneuvers under perturbations, while standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods are limited by low simulation throughput and poor sample efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a massively parallel DRL guidance framework. A fully tensorized, GPU-resident orbital propagator is developed to integrate $J_2$-perturbed orbital dynamics and policy optimization within a zero-copy pipeline, achieving up to a 67-fold increase in simulation throughput over conventional CPU baselines. In addition, the rendezvous problem is formulated in modified equinoctial elements and trained with a progressive curriculum learning strategy to improve convergence and generalization across increasingly challenging rendezvous scenarios. Simulations show that the proposed framework can learn robust rendezvous trajectories for complex multi-revolution rendezvous over a broad range of orbital configurations. Additional evaluations under a high-fidelity model and eclipse-induced thrust interruptions further demonstrate the robustness of the learned policy under practical mission constraints. Moreover, the trajectories generated by the proposed framework can be used as effective initial guesses for optimization-based trajectory solvers, improving the convergence of high-precision trajectory optimization. The method offers a scalable approach for real-time low-thrust guidance and trajectory optimization.
item.dc:creator: Chenglong Wu, Yi Zhou, Bin Cheng, Nan Zhang, Hexi Baoyin

item.title: Real-Time Threat Classification in Multi-Agent Systems via Topology-Coupled Hidden Markov Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.10779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Networked multi-agent systems coordinating in adversarial environments face compound cyber threats that alternate between false-data injection (FDI), denial-of-service (DoS), and stealthy decoy perturbations designed to mimic benign operational anomalies. Because the switching policy is latent and the plant dynamics evolve continuously, deterministic threshold detectors struggle to isolate deception without causing excessive false alarms. This paper presents an online, data-driven framework that couples distributed continuous time unknown input observers (UIOs) with a topology-aware Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for real-time attack detection and classification under unknown adversarial strategies. By decoupling FDI signals from augmented node states, distributed observers deployed across the network generate local augmented residuals that are discretized into emission sequences. The HMM embeds the underlying directed communication graph into the off-diagonal blocks of its transition probability matrix, explicitly capturing inter-agent attack propagation. Both transition and observation probabilities are updated recursively online via an Expectation-Maximization (EM) scheme, adapting the classifier to evolving threat behaviours without prior offline calibration. Numerical simulations on a directed network demonstrate that incorporating graph topology into the latent transition dynamics resolves the severe classification ambiguity between nominal and decoy modes, outperforming decoupled agent-independent decoders while restricting observer deployment to a sparse subset of nodes.
item.dc:creator: Ailin Barzegar, Davide Spinello, Mohammad Pirani

item.title: A Nested Heterogeneous Multiscale Framework for Power System Dynamic Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.10836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power system dynamics involve multiple timescales, from electromagnetic transients of the network and inverter-based resources to electromechanical oscillations of synchronous generators and quasi-steady-state evolution of the operating point. Simulating these dynamics with a detailed electromagnetic transient model is computationally prohibitive, whereas existing methods reduce the model to focus on a single timescale and lose accuracy when dynamics of different timescales interact. This paper proposes a nested heterogeneous multiscale framework for highly efficient multi-timescale simulation of a power system represented by one unified detailed model. Rather than varying only the integration step, the framework adaptively shifts the simulation resolution among three nested levels so that the dynamics of interest at each stage are always captured, with the slower dynamics estimated on the fly from short detailed simulations at controlled accuracy. Theoretical analysis proves the stability of long steps during quasi-steady-state evolution and quantifies the attainable speedup. On a modified IEEE 39-bus system with frequency regulation and load restoration, the framework accurately reproduces the dynamics of all timescales and runs 15 to 18 times faster than conventional simulation of the detailed model. The accuracy and speedup of the proposed method are further verified on a 390-bus system, demonstrating its scalability to large power systems.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyang Huang, Min Xiong, Yang Liu, Kai Sun

item.title: Computationally Efficient Data Generation for Learning Nonlinear MPC Policies
item.description: arXiv:2611.10897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning MPC requires large datasets generated by repeatedly solving MPC problems. For Nonlinear MPC (NMPC), dataset generation is computationally expensive because feasible initial states are difficult to sample efficiently. The feasible set is often non-convex or even disconnected, and many randomly sampled states are infeasible, leading to wasted optimization solves and unnecessary computational effort. In this work, we propose a data-generation framework for learning NMPC policies that combines active-set exploration with projection-based sampling. First, a bilevel formulation samples activity weights to promote solutions associated with different active sets while preserving optimality for the original NMPC problem; second, a simpler slack-based formulation uses weighted slack variables to target different active sets at the single level. These reference solutions are then used to construct local linearized feasible sets, from which candidate initial states are sampled and projected through the nonlinear NMPC problem to recover feasible and locally optimal training samples. Our approach is up to $37\times$ faster than baseline uniform sampling with $99\%$ acceptance rate, while maintaining a representative coverage of the feasible set.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Gori, Anton Pozharskiy, Franco Angelini, Manolo Garabini, Moritz Diehl, Armin Nurkanovi\'c

item.title: Bisect-Index-Choose: A Fast and Exact Algorithm for EV Charging under Minimum Charging Rates
item.description: arXiv:2611.10902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations are increasingly operated with an aggregate power limit below the sum of their port ratings, and require scheduling algorithms to divide the available power among the connected EVs. Charging standards permit a current that is either zero or at least a minimum rate, typically 6 A, which makes this allocation problem non-convex. Existing methods either solve a mixed-integer program with a commercial solver, which can be computationally expensive, adds software dependencies, and incurs licensing costs, or apply heuristics without optimality guarantees. This paper proposes Bisect-Index-Choose (BIC), a fast and solver-free scheduling algorithm that computes a globally optimal allocation among EVs under mild assumptions on their utilities. For $n$ EVs, BIC runs in $O(n \log n)$ time when all EVs share one maximum rate and in $O(n^2)$ time for two, times a logarithmic factor in the numerical precision. In tests with up to 1000 EVs, BIC attains global optimality and is up to three orders of magnitude faster than the solver. On real-world charging data, it needs less capacity and delivers more energy than existing heuristics. We implement BIC on a low-cost microcontroller and show that it solves instances with 1000 EVs in less than 90 ms.
item.dc:creator: Can Berk Saner

item.title: An Interline Multiport DC Circuit Breaker with Power Flow Controller
item.description: arXiv:2611.10980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Currently, the high-voltage multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids face two major challenges. First, fast rise rate and lack of zero-crossing point in DC-side fault currents render AC circuit breakers inoperable. Second, DC line currents are passively determined by terminal DC voltages and line resistances, which inherently limits the capability of changing individual line currents for essential grid services such as power flow management and overloading prevention. To address these two limitations, DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) and DC power flow controllers (DCPFCs) have been developed. The conventional DCCBs are two-port devices installed in series with DC lines at their terminals in an MTDC converter substation, so that any fault current flowing through the line can be rapidly cleared. Additionally, a DCPFC can be installed at line terminals to adjust terminal voltages and power exchanges among adjacent lines. As a result, for a substation that connects to multiple lines, it needs to host multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, which significantly increases the cost and footprint of both the substation and the MTDC grid. To this end, this work proposes an integrated equipment combining multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, called the interline multiport DCCB with DCPFC, which can reduce the number of components and enhance the economic feasibility of MTDC networks. This paper presents the topology, operation principles, and component selection procedures of the proposed equipment, and compares it with the state-of-the-art technologies. Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation results validate the fault interruption and power flow control performance of the interline multiport DCCB with PFC.
item.dc:creator: Maliha Ferdous, Zhi Jin Zhang, Qichen Yang, Maryam Saeedifard

item.title: Feasibility-Aware Learning for Network-Constrained Unit Commitment
item.description: arXiv:2611.11101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning-based approaches to network-constrained unit commitment (NCUC) usually still rely on an optimization solver to repair or complete their predictions, which limits the speedup they can deliver. This paper proposes FALCON-UC, a feasibility-aware graph learning framework that predicts commitment and dispatch jointly and produces final schedules without solving a mixed-integer program at inference time. It combines an LSTM--GraphSAGE predictor over a fully connected generator graph, a differentiable correction that embeds commitment-dependent dispatch bounds, power balance, and PTDF-based branch flows in training, and deterministic commitment, dispatch, and ramp-coupled reserve repairs at inference. On the 2383-bus system, FALCON-UC achieves $99.09\%$ commitment accuracy and a $0.4350\%$ mean absolute cost gap with all evaluated constraints within tolerance at $0.0562$ s per instance, a $2.27\times10^{3}$ speedup over the solver. MTLR R-SCUC-FL is slightly more accurate but still needs an optimization solver to complete each schedule, which takes $262.2$ s per instance, $4.67\times10^{3}$ times the FALCON-UC runtime. A label-only baseline without repair violates the balance and branch limits on every 2383-bus test instance, and FALCON-UC also meets all evaluated constraint tolerances on a 1354-bus system.
item.dc:creator: Hien Thanh Doan, Yeji Lim, Hongseok Kim

item.title: Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
item.description: arXiv:2611.11119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning-based safety certification offers a promising route for verifying complex dynamical systems when explicit models are unavailable, but existing data-driven methods often scale poorly: they treat the system as a black box, rely on dense discretizations or Lipschitz bounds, and consequently suffer from sample complexity that grows exponentially with dimension. This paper shows that a common structural property of dynamical systems--monotonicity--can be used to break this curse of dimensionality. We develop a data-driven framework for robust safety verification and safe controller synthesis for unknown monotone systems using only simulator queries. Our main theoretical result proves that, for monotone systems with upper-closed unsafe sets, safety is completely characterized by the existence of monotone inductive barrier certificates. This structure reduces certificate verification over continuous state spaces to localized boundary checks over finitely many cells. To learn such certificates, we introduce Max-Monotone Networks, a monotone neural architecture with universal approximation guarantees for monotone functions. We then propose a training and refinement algorithm that, upon successful termination, returns formally valid neural barrier certificates and, under mild partition assumptions, requires only $O(n)$ simulator queries. Across high-dimensional benchmarks, including oscillator networks with up to $13{,}659$ states and traffic networks with $1{,}000$ states, our method certifies safety in regimes where prior approaches either do not converge or exceed memory limits. These results demonstrate that exploiting order structure can make neural safety certification both scalable and formally sound.
item.dc:creator: Amirreza Alavi, Majid Zamani, Saber Jafarpour

item.title: Learning the NMPC with Stability Guarantees
item.description: arXiv:2611.11163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) is widely used, its online optimization is computationally expensive. Neural network approximations of NMPC can effectively reduce the online computational burden but generally lack stability guarantees. This paper proposes an approximate NMPC framework with guarantees of constraint satisfaction and closed-loop stability. The approximation error is addressed through constraint tightening, and the resulting tightened NMPC is used to generate the training dataset of the approximate NMPC. The maximum allowable approximation error is prescribed a priori for the design of tightened NMPC and satisfied in a probabilistic sense through an iterative trial-and-error procedure alternating between network training and a posteriori verification. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through a numerical example of a constrained nonlinear system.
item.dc:creator: Shuyou Yu, Yan Sun, Jun Ai, Qifang Liu, Hong Chen

item.title: Numerical Stability Issues and a Mitigation Method in Switching Events Calculation Considering State Variable Discontinuities for EMT Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.11167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Some existing methods for switching events calculation considering state variable discontinuities for EMT simulation can encounter numerical stability issues, either over-stabilizing or destabilizing the studied power systems. This paper documents these issues in detail with a concrete example. The underlying mechanism of the issues are revealed via systematic analysis. A mitigation method for the issues is proposed. The convergence behavior of the method is analyzed. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. It is observed that the method also helps to improve the accuracy of the simulation results.
item.dc:creator: Sheng Lei

item.title: Spot Markets for AI Inference: Dynamic Capacity Allocation and Pricing on a Shared Accelerator Fleet
item.description: arXiv:2611.11215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inference providers size their accelerator fleets for the interactive peak and sell spare capacity through fixed discounts, such as batch tiers at half price. However, inference differs from conventional cloud capacity in four respects: capacity depends on the latency tier through batching, moving weights between models is slow and costly, spot demand can wait until its deadline, and power can bind. In this paper, we develop a framework for dynamic capacity allocation and pricing of AI inference on a shared accelerator fleet. We consider a provider that serves several models under a power cap and sells each model in an interactive tier with a speed promise and in a spot tier for preemptible work with a deadline. In each period, the provider chooses how many replicas of each model to keep loaded and what spot price to quote. We show that one interactive token displaces a fixed number $\rho_m>1$ of spot tokens, and that the optimal spot price lies midway between the interactive price and the effective cost of capacity in the deadline window, which is close to the prevailing half price only when the fleet is slack. We further show that a spot tier raises the optimal reliability of the interactive tier, and that placement should follow persistent demand shifts while prices absorb transients. Building on these results, we design a model predictive controller based on a linear program with explicit approximation bounds, which solves each period in milliseconds. Numerical experiments on a simulated week with a measured daily demand profile, a flash crowd, and a grid curtailment show that the controller raises profit by 7.4% over fixed half-price practice, captures 93% of the gain available with perfect forecasts, keeps the interactive promise through both events, and leaves spot buyers better off.
item.dc:creator: Quanyan Zhu

item.title: Grid-forming Control of Offshore Wind through a Diode-Rectifier HVDC System: a 2 GW Case Study
item.description: arXiv:2611.11221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diode-rectifier-unit (DRU)-based high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission considerably reduces the volume and weight of the offshore converter platform for remote wind farms and, hence, its cost, but shifts the task of forming and regulating the offshore AC network to the wind-turbine converters. This paper examines which grid-forming control strategy is the most suitable for DRU power transfer. The DRU commutation relationship shows that the delivered active power depends on the offshore voltage magnitude (but not on the converter voltage angle), so the angle-based active-power loop of virtual synchronous machine control is not closed through the rectifier. A $P-V/Q-{\omega}$ grid-forming architecture, which regulates active power via the voltage magnitude and derives frequency from the reactive power error, is therefore adopted. Electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1GWaggregated grid-forming turbine on a 66 kV collector network with a $\pm$525 kV bipolar DRU link show that the commanded power is delivered over 800 to 1000MW with the offshore voltage held near nominal. The paper also examines how grid-forming operation changes the allocation of control duties within the Type-4 turbine: once the grid-side converter forms the network, DC link regulation must move to the machine-side converter, which limits the achievable bandwidth of the DC-link control. Extending the system to 2 GW with two 500 MW grid-following units achieves full power transfer in simulation, but with the grid-forming converter loaded beyond its continuous rating and a steady-state offshore frequency deviation of approximately 1.8 Hz.
item.dc:creator: Ishi Nigam, Saif Alsarayreh, Tuanku Badzlin Hashfi, Milo\v{s} Cvetkovi\'c, Joris van Doorn, Aleksandra Leki\'c

item.title: GFM Control Automatic Compliance Toolbox
item.description: arXiv:2611.11229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing penetration of converter-interfaced generation reduces system inertia, short-circuit strength, and voltage support. European grid codes, including the ENTSO-E Network Code on Requirements for Generators and the ACER Demand Connection Code, now define disturbance-based validation procedures for grid-forming (GFM) generation and converter-based demand. Commercial RMS tools, however, lack an integrated workflow aligned with these recent requirements. This paper presents an automated Python-PowerFactory compliance toolbox and an RMS test bench for a co-located system comprising a 1 MW GFM photovoltaic (PV) plant, a 0.3 MW GFM battery energy storage system (BESS), and a 1 MW converter-interfaced dynamic load at a 20 kV point of common coupling fed from a 110 kV grid. Extended virtual synchronous machine models and a DCC-oriented load model are tested in batch, with results automatically extracted and plotted for assessment. Results show compliant RMS performance for the slower, electromechanical tests, while the paper identifies which tests require complementary electromagnetic transient (EMT) verification.
item.dc:creator: Tejas Kunbi, Rahul Rane, Dan Wu, Aleksandra Leki\'c

item.title: Scenario-Based Assessment of Transport Electrification for Low-Carbon Urban Planning: A Case Study of Phu Quoc, Vietnam
item.description: arXiv:2611.11377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Urban net-zero strategies require a defensible emissions boundary and quantitative estimates of the contribution achievable through individual mitigation measures. This study assesses road-transport electrification within a planned residential development in Phu Quoc, Vietnam, using the assumptions and scenario data of an urban-planning study originally prepared in 2022. A vehicle-class inventory combines population-dependent fleet projections, assumed travel activity, gasoline and diesel consumption, fuel-specific carbon dioxide (CO_2) factors, and electricity-related emissions from battery-electric vehicles. The reference case projects annual road-transport emissions of 59.41, 73.86, and 87.23 tCO_2 for 2022, 2025, and 2030, respectively. Three year-specific substitution scenarios, corresponding to nominal electric-vehicle shares of 25%, 50%, and 100%, yield source-reported avoided emissions of 9.43, 13.64, and 55.41 tCO_2/year, or 15.9%, 18.5%, and 63.5% of their respective baselines. However, a cross-scenario audit identifies an inconsistency in the 2025 mixed-fleet results under time-invariant vehicle-class emission-intensity ratios: under that additional assumption, 2025 avoided emissions would be 23.45 rather than 13.64 tCO_2/year. The original detailed vehicle-energy input tables are not included in the available source document, preventing definitive reconciliation. The study therefore provides a transparent, preliminary planning assessment rather than evidence of citywide net-zero attainment. Its principal value is a reproducible accounting structure and an explicit identification of the data, electricity-system, and infrastructure constraints that must be resolved before policy or investment decisions.
item.dc:creator: Tien-Khai Nguyen

item.title: A Distributed Observer with Random Agent Activations over Random Communication Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.11392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a distributed observer for the forward-Euler discretization of a continuous-time linear time-invariant system under random local operations and random communications. Under uniform stochastic strong connectivity, we establish almost sure exponential convergence of all local state estimates for sufficiently small discretization step sizes. We further examine how the underlying parameters and components affect the admissible range of the discretization step size and the guaranteed convergence rate bound. Unlike related approaches, the proposed method does not require each local unobservable subspace to admit an $A$-invariant complement.
item.dc:creator: Yong Joo Do, Jin Gyu Lee

item.title: Local Certificate Repair for Asynchronous Controller Updates in Recommender Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.11462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how to adapt an existing distributed recommendation controller when local dynamics or objective weights change. Starting from a quadratic stability and cost certificate, we construct positive semidefinite corrections with finite spatial support and an explicit residual. A joint admission test allocates the available dissipation margin to these residuals and to interactions among changes and corrections, including pending updates. The test covers complete declared parameter ranges, allowing different operators to progress independently. For a fixed compatible batch, the corrections define a common storage that guarantees exponential stability and bounds the cost accumulated throughout deployment. When the admitted collection evolves, a reservation protocol preserves the certificate and a rate bound on storage increases ensures exponential convergence. Regional linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) design proposes new gain rows for the operators' own users, and a separate residual-based calculation can certify that the final gain lowers the expected cost. A recommendation-network example illustrates the tradeoff between repair depth, data access, and the benefits of deploying an update.
item.dc:creator: Simone Mariano, Paolo Frasca

item.title: Ultrawideband Polarization-Rotating Antenna for Enhanced Ground Penetrating Radar Detection
item.description: arXiv:2611.11523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) represents a powerful and widely adopted tool for nondestructive subsurface detection and imaging. To overcome the impaired detection performance caused by polarization mismatch in conventional single-channel GPR systems, this paper presents an innovative ultrawideband polarization-rotating (UPR) antenna that achieves rotating linear polarizations (LPs) by varying the source frequency for enhanced detection. The developed UPR antenna achieves a continuous polarization rotation from $0^\circ$ to $170^\circ$ across 1.2 to 3.2 GHz, as verified by both full-wave simulations and experimental measurements. The antenna is subsequently integrated into a single-channel stepped-frequency GPR system and evaluated against targets of varying geometries in a sandy environment. Compared with a conventional fixed-LP GPR system, the UPR antenna-enabled GPR system delivers markedly more consistent detection performance across all target types, with particularly pronounced enhancements for polarization-sensitive targets. By enabling ultrawideband frequency-dependent polarization agility, the proposed GPR system enhances subsurface target detection while maintaining the simplicity and low cost of a single-channel measurement architecture.
item.dc:creator: Ming Li, Yuki Gao, Shu-Lin Chen, Hai-Han Sun, Y. Jay Guo

item.title: Concurrent Learning-Based Inertial Parameter Estimation and Control of Quadrotors
item.description: arXiv:2611.11555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this letter, we consider trajectory tracking control and inertial parameter estimation of a quadrotor UAV whose center of mass (CoM) does not coincide with its geometric center. Onboard payloads like an IMU, a camera, or a battery are not necessarily placed at its geometric center. Moreover, during the flight these sensors might move because of external disturbances and cause a CoM offset. Thus, these events and equipment introduce an offset and cause the inertia matrix to be non-diagonal. We develop an integral concurrent learning (ICL)-based geometric controller that estimates the mass, the CoM offset, and the full inertia matrix online, without an accelerometer or numerical derivatives, and tracks a given trajectory corrected by the offset estimated online. We prove that the estimated parameters converge to their true values under a finite excitation condition. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm using a simulation example.
item.dc:creator: Sandesh Thapa, He Bai

item.title: Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.11634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.
item.dc:creator: Changrui Liu, Robin Wroblowski, Anil Alan, Shengling Shi, Rodolphe Sepulchre, Bart De Schutter

item.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.11716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. The topology exploits this: a thermoelectric thin film lies flat on a diamond substrate beside the device drain (the electron exit), so bulk Joule heat leaves vertically into the substrate. A lateral fin model gives a closed form for the recirculation factor gamma: the vertical pillar yields gamma = 1, while the horizontal film yields gamma_max = sqrt(2) L_z/L_x, about 0.03 for L_z = 10 um, L_x = 500 um. The decoupling scales the net cooling ceiling and the critical runaway current by roughly 1/gamma. At equal resistance, the same film lifts maximum cooling from 13 mW to 500 mW, and the critical current from 0.65 A to 24 A. A time-constant and linear stability analysis with temperature-sensitive parameters defines the working window and safety margins for microsecond pulse cooling. The architecture leaves the device structure untouched; the principle, absorb at an interface and extract bulk heat vertically, applies to any chip with a hot core and offers a reproducible design path for near-junction thermal management.
item.dc:creator: Xiangying Li

item.title: Scarcity Pricing for State-of-Charge Management in Real-Time Markets Under Intra-Day Uncertainty
item.description: arXiv:2611.11730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growth in renewable resources will increase net load variability and forecast error. Energy storage resources can provide flexibility when ramp capability is limited and contribute to load leveling over the day. The challenge for system operators is how to balance these two functions in real time, when updated net load forecasts are available for a limited lookahead horizon. U.S. electricity markets are seeking ways to manage state-of-charge (SoC) within their energy markets to more efficiently utilize these resources. We propose a method to manage energy storage SoC in a real-time market by extending Hogan's (2013) scarcity pricing framework. A day-ahead SoC schedule is modified using existing multi-interval real-time unit commitment engines as net load forecasts change. To address 30-minute-ahead forecast errors, an updated 5-minute SoC target and a dynamically updated shortage price for violating the constraint are provided to each economic dispatch. We simulate PJM's energy markets for 365 days and demonstrate reliability improvements relative to a strategy that enforces the day-ahead schedule. We show cost reductions and improved price formation relative to a strategy that updates target quantities but uses an administratively chosen shortage penalty.
item.dc:creator: Shailesh Wasti, Aravind Retna Kumar, Sushant Varghese, Anthony Giacomoni, Parviz Alivand, Yujie Hu, Mort Webster

item.title: MAC+: Mobility-Aware Co-Expansion Planning for Distribution Grid and Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.11791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the least-cost co-expansion of power distribution networks and public charging ports to accommodate the growth of electric vehicles (EVs). Our approach, MAC+, exploits the flexibility of charging along each EV's itinerary and coordinates it across the fleet to reduce the peak violations of each feeder's hosting capacity and port capacity. This coordination is an extremely large, spatio-temporally coupled optimization problem with binary plug-in variables. We solve it by iterated price response (IPR), which repeatedly posts a two-tier tariff on feeder load and port occupancy, lets millions of EVs best-respond in parallel, and certifies the optimality gap at every iteration. We develop a custom exact dynamic-programming algorithm that solves each EV's best-response problem, a mixed-integer quadratic program, about 20 times faster than off-the-shelf solvers. The case study covers the San Francisco Bay Area at 30% EV adoption, with 1.8 million EVs on week-long itineraries and 1,303 feeder service regions, each with a utility-published hosting capacity and a port capacity set by its existing public ports. On this instance, IPR reaches a certified gap below 10% in a few hours. MAC+ saves about $15 billion of the upgrade investment that unmanaged charging would require. It also needs over 90% less investment than charging that is fully coordinated but flexible only within each session, and over 80% less than charging that is flexible along the itinerary but uncoordinated.
item.dc:creator: Yi Ju, Lunlong Li, Jingchun Wang, Scott Moura

item.title: Generalizable Output Feedback Optimal Control via Transformers Without Explicit State Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.11815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical optimal control is used to design a separate controller for each plant. This paper asks a different question. Can one learned policy serve a whole family of partially observed, noisy linear systems? We show that one transformer can. The policy is trained to imitate optimal LQG control on a heterogeneous family of Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems with Multiple Inputs and Multiple Outputs (MIMO), whose dimensions, cost matrices, and noise levels all vary. A shared representation with system-wise standardization, zero-padding, masking, and an encoding of the cost and noise covariances lets one set of weights control every member of the family. At run time, a short window of noisy measurements is all the policy needs to produce a control action, with no plant matrices and no state estimator. We characterize the relation between the optimal LQG policy (represented as a dynamic state-space model) and a static transformer acting on a finite window of measurements. We then express the closed-loop excess cost of any causal policy as the energy of its deviation from the optimal action. Finally, we evaluate the approach on 28 simulated systems. The trained policy reaches the optimal cost to within a median gap of $0.4\%$ for seen systems. For unseen systems, a light fine-tuning step brings the median gap to $1.0\%$.
item.dc:creator: Maitham F. AL-Sunni, Turki Bin Mohaya, John M. Dolan, Peter Seiler

item.title: One number per hour is not enough: directional carbon intensity of data-center ramps on the PJM fleet
item.description: arXiv:2611.12056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A data-center campus can change its load by hundreds of megawatts within an hour, yet every carbon signal in use gives one value per hour for a load change, whatever its size or direction. We compute the directional carbon intensity, the emission caused or avoided per megawatt-hour of a finite upward or downward ramp, for every hour of 2025 on the PJM Interconnection's fossil fleet, and compare it with the locational marginal emission rate (LME) and the regional average. The LME misstates a 1 GW ramp by more than 10% in 60% to 83% of hours in eleven months. Upward and downward ramps differ in a quarter to three quarters of hours but agree on their monthly mean. Location-based reporting assigns 47% to 59% of a ramp's emission to other consumers. A campus should schedule on the signal for its ramp's size and direction and report the emission it causes.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoying Shi, Jinyue Yan

item.title: DC Voltage Control Dominated Oscillations in Electromechanical Frequency Range - Insights from Synchronous Coefficient Reduction Effect of IBR Plants and Network Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.12192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) is widely known to cause subsynchronous oscillations. This paper investigates a distinct class of oscillations that occur in the electromechanical frequency range (EFR), referred to as EFOs, and are dominated by the DC voltage control (DVC) loops of grid-following IBRs rather than synchronous generator-like controls or phase-locked loops (PLLs). Although open-loop oscillation modes of DVC loops are subsynchronous, the corresponding closed-loop dominant oscillation mode related to DVC can shift downward into the EFR without retuning the control parameters. This frequency shift is caused by network-mediated interactions among the IBRs, which introduce a negative synchronous coefficient into the DVC oscillation loop. This synchronous coefficient reduction effect (SCRE) becomes stronger as the IBR plant scale increases and/or as the minimum eigenvalue of the network admittance matrix decreases. Furthermore, a complex vector-based stability analysis method is proposed, and a stability criterion for DVC-EFOs is derived. Finally, the analytical conclusions are validated using a practical power system configuration implemented in Simulink. The SCRE differs from traditional explanations, in which the open-loop oscillation modes are already located in the EFR, and provides new insight into DVC-dominated oscillations in the EFR for integration of IBR plants.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Fu, Siqi Bu

item.title: Environmental Assessment of GaN Current-Source and Voltage-Source AC-AC Variable Speed Drives
item.description: arXiv:2611.12211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Three-phase ac-ac converters for variable-speed drives can be realized conventionally as voltage-source converters (VSCs) or, leveraging emerging monolithic bidirectional GaN power transistors (M-BDSs), as current-source converters (CSCs). This paper presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of a realized VSC and a CSC demonstrators including grid-side and motor-side EMI filters, and with identical specifications (1.4 kW rated power, 200 V line-to-line rms grid and motor voltage). The embodied carbon footprints are similar (44.8 kgCO2eq for the VSC and 47.4 kgCO2eq for the CSC) and dominated by auxiliary and control electronics, and the printed circuit boards. Over 10 years of continuous operation under the NEMA Power Index mission profile for variable-load centrifugal systems (pumps, fans), the CSC's higher part-load efficiency translates into a clearly lower life-cycle carbon footprint of around 900 kgCO2eq compared to the VSC's 1130 kgCO2eq when operating with a carbon-intense electricity mix (440 gCO2eq/kWh). However, this difference almost vanishes when considering a future renewable electricity mix (25 gCO2eq/kWh).
item.dc:creator: Luc Imperiali, Jonas Huber

item.title: Prospective Action-Resource Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Electric HGV Fleets under Shared Charging Infrastructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.12244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electric heavy goods vehicle (eHGV) fleet coordination requires each vehicle to choose driving, charging and resting actions whose consequences depend on shared infrastructure. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods mainly represent current states, leaving action-specific futures and resource interactions to be learned indirectly. We develop Horizon-Preview and Graph-Coordinated Proximal Policy Optimisation (HGC-PPO), which integrates horizon preview and candidate-resource graph coordination into the PPO decision architecture. Horizon preview represents each legal action through its short-horizon operational consequences. Graph message passing then updates these candidates through station, charger-type and time-slot resources shared across the fleet. On the 794km Folkestone-Glasgow task, HGC-PPO achieved the lowest mean charging cost among five RL methods at {\pounds}504.32 per vehicle, with a fleet completion time of 24.920h. It also completed the task 1.763h faster and cost {\pounds}36.51 less per vehicle than a replay-verified finite-budget MILP benchmark. Across six unseen routes and fleet sizes from 5 to 20 vehicles, HGC-PPO delivered the lowest macro-average completion time, charging cost and charging frequency among the RL methods. A 2 by 2 ablation showed that the full preview-graph architecture performed best across all four operational metrics. These results show that prospective action information and fleet-wide resource coordination improve eHGV decisions under charging and driver-hours constraints.
item.dc:creator: Yiming Xu, Fulong Yao, Maurizio Albano, Rigel Gjomemo, Liana Cipcigan

item.title: A Scale-Space Theory of Memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.12316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scale-space theory has emerged as a central attempt to restrict the {\it general} theory of signal processing with geometric constraints inspired from the animal world. In the mathematical language of operator theory, scale-space theory restricts the Toeplitz operator. The present paper investigates scale-space theory for memory systems. We investigate how scale space theory restricts a memory system encoding past information, that is, restricts the Hankel operator. Our main result is to establish a close correspondence between scale-space theory and the long-studied {\it relaxation} property.
item.dc:creator: Dongjun Wu, Rodolphe Sepulchre

item.title: Tensor Network Kernel Machines for Nonlinear System Identification
item.description: arXiv:2611.12326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over the past ten years Tensor Network Kernel Machines have enabled efficient nonlinear system identification through the use of low-rank tensor networks. The goal of this article is to provide the reader with a basic understanding of this model class in terms of its two defining properties. Furthermore, both the optimization and regularization of such models are discussed, together with recent developments and starting points for further exploration.
item.dc:creator: Kim Batselier

item.title: Observer-based parameter estimation in a Darcy model towards dam internal seepage monitoring with validation on real data
item.description: arXiv:2611.12403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses internal seepage monitoring in hydraulic infrastructures through the estimation of physical parameters in a distributed model. A physics-based approach relying on Darcy's law is adopted to describe the spatiotemporal evolution of hydraulic head within the structure. To enable real-time applicability, a Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) is employed to derive a reduced-order model of the underlying partial differential equation. An Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is then designed to perform online estimation of the hydraulic diffusivity, a key parameter related to the structural state. The proposed method is validated directly on real measurement data through a twofold approach. First, the estimated parameter is compared with the value obtained via offline batch optimization performed on the same dataset, showing consistent results. Second, the ability of the resulting model, parametrized by the estimated diffusivity, to reconstruct the observed measurements is assessed, to evaluate its suitability for seepage monitoring.

item.title: Sensor placement for real-life water distribution networks, ensuring observability under uncertainties
item.description: arXiv:2611.12414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Leakage detection in water distribution networks (WDNs) is crucial for limiting water losses. However, effective detection strongly depends on sensor availability and placement. Most existing sensor placement methods rely on extensive simulations or precise knowledge of hydraulic parameters, which are often uncertain in practice. In this paper, we propose using a scalable sensor placement framework based on structural observability that depends only on the network topology and the underlying pressure-flow interconnection structure. The approach guarantees structural observability independently of hydraulic parameters, and is therefore robust to parametric uncertainties, assuming that the network topology is correctly specified. The method is computationally efficient and its performance is demonstrated on several real-life WDNs provided by Brabant-Water. While the framework ensures full network observability, the required number of sensors can be high in large and cyclic networks, which may limit applicability in real-life and motivates future work on relaxed observability guarantees for sensor placement.
item.dc:creator: Jarne J. H. van Gemert, Valentina Breschi, Claudia Quintiliani, Doekle R. Yntema, Karel J. Keesman, Mircea Lazar

item.title: Scalable Practical Synchronization of Heterogeneous Linear Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study practical state synchronization of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems over directed graphs using static diffusive state feedback. Persistent mismatches between the agent dynamics generally preclude exact synchronization and are treated as bounded disturbances within an Input-to-State Stability (ISS) framework. We derive a scalable synthesis procedure based on fixed-dimension linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), whose dimension is independent of the number of agents. Local robust dissipation conditions are combined through a small-gain argument to obtain global ISS guarantees and explicit bounds on the synchronization error. The framework is formulated in a unified manner for continuous- and discrete-time systems, while highlighting a fundamental difference in disturbance attenuation between the two domains. In particular, exact ZOH discretization of a continuous-time controller need not preserve closed-loop stability, motivating a native discrete-time synthesis. Numerical experiments on heterogeneous harmonic oscillators illustrate the proposed approach and the continuous/discrete-time distinction.
item.dc:creator: Alex Ardelean (DANCE), Giacomo Casadei (GIPSA-lab,DANCE,GIPSA-PAD), Paolo Frasca (DANCE)

item.title: KPG193-ext: A Synthetic Korean Power Grid Test System for Stability Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.12439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Growing shares of inverter-based generation and constrained transmission expansion increase the need to assess stability across operating conditions. Production-cost models provide chronological commitment and dispatch, but stability analysis requires corresponding electrical detail and device dynamics. This paper introduces KPG193-ext, an extension of the synthetic Korean power-grid test system KPG193 that links chronological operating points with detailed electrical and dynamic models. The extension adds synchronous-machine, controller and renewable-converter models, together with explicit voltage levels, generation terminals, inter-voltage and step-up transformers, and reactive compensation. The resulting 731-bus network retains the original 193 regional locations. Daily unit commitment followed by hourly AC optimal power flow establishes 8,760 operating points for 2025, each distributed as paired steady-state and dynamic-model files. Selected-hour studies examine generation-loss frequency response, steady-state flow-voltage characteristics, and rotor-angle response with special protection system actions. The results reveal differences in delivered frequency support, internal voltage stress along regional transfer paths, and the angle-frequency tradeoff of corrective generator tripping. The database provides a common basis for examining the stability implications of commitment, dispatch and corrective action across daily and seasonal operating conditions.
item.dc:creator: Sungyoon Song, Geonho Song, Min-han Yoon, Yong-Hyun Song, Seung Wan Kim, Jip Kim

item.title: Towards Passivity-informed Data-driven Predictive Control
item.description: arXiv:2611.12531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a passivity-informed data-driven predictive control framework based on passivity-preserving sampling of unknown continuous-time linear systems. We incorporate the passive supply rate into the objective functional alongside an output-regulation cost, thereby explicitly accounting for energy extraction. Despite being practically motivated, the resulting objective is not always convex; its convexity depends on the collected input-output training data. We exploit passivity-induced positive semidefiniteness to derive an equivalent reformulation that remains a convex quadratic program independently of the data. Furthermore, we establish recursive feasibility and asymptotic output convergence using passivity and a terminal equality constraint. Numerical simulations illustrate the closed-loop performance and computational benefits of the proposed approach.
item.dc:creator: Guanru Pan, Oleksii Molodchyk, Mohammad Itani, Timm Faulwasser

item.title: Degradation-Aware Participation of Battery Storage in Frequency Regulation Markets
item.description: arXiv:2611.12555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As data centers make the load on the power grid fluctuate faster, frequency regulation grows more valuable. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are well suited to provide frequency regulation, but providing this service speeds up aging, especially during operation at extreme state of charge (SoC). In the PJM interconnection, the grid operator supplies a regulation signal that a participating BESS is expected to follow, within a capacity that it must bid before the signal is known. Accordingly, we decompose the degradation-aware frequency regulation problem into a bidding layer and an operations layer. For bidding, we propose an adaptive strategy, assuming perfect tracking in which the bid depends on the SoC expected at the start of the bid period by means of choosing basepoints. For operation, the BESS further protects its battery by deliberately giving up a perfect performance score, to keep its SoC away from the extremes. On the PJM regulation signal and prices of 2023, adaptive bids lengthen the battery life by $31\%$ against bidding full capacity, for $2.2\%$ of the revenue. Giving up a perfect score in operation lengthens the battery life of constant bids by $10\%$ to $27\%$, at a change in revenue of at most $0.2\%$.
item.dc:creator: Anand Gokhale, Siddharth Bhela

item.title: Covert System Identification Under Timing Constraints: A Static Linear Model and Its Detectability Implications
item.description: arXiv:2611.12579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies covert system identification in cyber-physical systems, where an attacker infers plant dynamics while attempting to remain stealthy. We introduce a lightweight static linear model in which the time to execute a setpoint change is proportional to the commanded speed difference. On a Siemens PROFINET testbed this gain captures the drive's ramp response accurately but not its terminal overshoot. That omitted transient becomes the attacker's main exposure: on real traces, the residual left by the linear masking procedure is detected by two anomaly monitors, Process-Aware Stealthy-Attack Detection (PASAD) and the CUSUM change detector. Across the cascade identification and staircase attack strategies defined in the paper, the stealth boundary relates to the plant's own settling transients, a structural limit for this class of models under the adopted detector-calibration regime. Comparison against dynamic models obtained by N4SID, trained at multiple excitation amplitudes, shows that the evaluated N4SID models do not improve stealth over the structure-informed ramp model. Since per-cycle computation is negligible for both procedures, the binding trade-off is not inference cost but whether the attacker can acquire and refresh a model without injecting detectable perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Victor Mattos, Guilherme Sobreira, Amit Bhaya, Alan Oliveira de S\'a, Charles B. Prado, Raphael Machado, Gaurav Srivastava, Daniel S. Menasche

item.title: Reshaping Checkpoint-Induced Power Variations Through Inference Workload Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2611.12621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synchronous checkpoints in large language model training cause rapid power variations that challenge frequency regulation in islanded data-center microgrids. This paper proposes a checkpoint-aware two-layer framework that schedules flexible inference workloads to compensate for checkpoint-induced disturbances. Using measured GPU power profiles and anticipated checkpoint power deficits, the upper layer coordinates heterogeneous task selection and launch times, while the lower layer adjusts the batch sizes of newly launched tasks online to correct power-tracking errors. Early launching (EL) and staged retirement (SR) further smooth power transitions at checkpoint onset and recovery, respectively. PSCAD/EMTDC simulations with reference checkpoint drops of 1-3 MW demonstrate reductions of 41.6-61.6% in maximum absolute frequency deviation and 68.5-89.6% in mean absolute frequency deviation relative to no scheduling. Battery energy storage system (BESS) peak charging power and charging energy decrease by 65.1-100% and 89.7-100%, respectively. These benefits exceed those of greedy scheduling when GPU resources are relatively abundant.
item.dc:creator: Yu Ma, Ziheng Sheng, Anna Andriiko, Chau-Wai Wong, Jong Ha Woo, Zishuo Yang, Aaditya Pandey, Wenyuan Tang, Ning Lu

item.title: Offset-Free Data-Driven Predictive Control: Implicit and Explicit Disturbance Formulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Offset-free tracking is a key objective of any control algorithm. For predictive controllers with linear models, it is well understood that rejecting asymptotically-constant disturbances necessitates augmenting the prediction model with $p$ integrating states, where $p$ is the number of measured outputs. This can be achieved in model predictive control (MPC) by using a velocity form or a combination of disturbance model and observer. In data-driven predictive control (DPC), implicit incorporation of integrating states using the velocity form has been successfully adopted to obtain offset-free tracking; however, formulations based on an explicit disturbance model and observer have not yet been explored. In this paper, we first study how the integrating states are incorporated into the data-based representation used in DPC, translating the requirements of $p$ integrating states into the required modifications of the DPC formulation. We then propose a novel offset-free DPC formulation that incorporates an explicit constant output-disturbance model and an output disturbance observer. Numerical examples show that this formulation has similar disturbance-rejection capabilities to the velocity-form DPC, but using a smaller optimisation problem.
item.dc:creator: Lucca Heinze Faro, Yuanbo Nie, Paul Trodden

item.title: Hierarchical Nonlinear Control for Swarm Encirclement Around a Moving Target UAV
item.description: arXiv:2611.12684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical inner-outer loop nonlinear control strategy using a geometric Lyapunov-based framework for the cooperative encirclement of a target by multi-ple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in three-dimensional space. The encirclement problem is formulated on a two-sphere with arbitrary radius and center, denoted Gamma-2, by projecting agent positions from R3 onto a spherical manifold centered at the target, being the unit two-sphere at the origin S2 used for intermediate calculations. Desired encirclement configurations are generated via a point separation method on Gamma-2, while stable convergence from R3 to these points is guaranteed using a Lyapunov-based reduced-attitude control law inspired by geometric control on the two-sphere. Formal stability results are derived using Lyapunov analysis and the framework is validated in simulation using a nonlinear quadrotor model and controller. Results demonstrate stable encirclement and highlight the suitability of the proposed approach for three-dimensional multi-agent aerial systems.
item.dc:creator: Filipe S. Cavalheiro, Bruno J. Guerreiro

item.title: Certified Zonotopic Reachability Analysis for Trajectory Tracking on Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.12767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous vehicles track planned trajectories close to obstacles. Unknown disturbances make them deviate from these trajectories. With a bound on the tracking error that disturbances can cause, a planned trajectory can be certified as safe before execution. Existing set-based methods bound the tracking error by one invariant ellipsoid for the whole trajectory or by intervals, which are both conservative. For aerial and space vehicles, the tracking error evolves on a matrix Lie group with nonlinear dynamics. However, for group-affine systems, the error dynamics are linear in Lie algebra coordinates when the vehicle receives the inputs of the reference. The control input and the disturbance enter through the inverse right Jacobian, a matrix that depends on the error. We propagate the linear part of the error dynamics with zonotopes and enclose the effect of the inverse right Jacobian on the disturbance in closed form. The resulting tubes are tight and provably contain all reachable tracking errors in continuous time. When some error components have no input, the inverse right Jacobian leaves unmatched nonlinear terms in the closed loop. None of the tested methods certifies such a closed loop. Hybrid coordinates make these terms matched, so that our controller cancels every nonlinear term that does not contain the disturbance. Our tubes give tighter bounds than the ellipsoid method in simulations of a planar aircraft and a fully actuated multirotor and in real flights of a quadrotor, where the tube contains every measured attitude error. Under larger disturbances and the same feedback gain, the ellipsoid method yields no valid ellipsoid, whereas our tubes remain valid.
item.dc:creator: Yanliang Huang, Peng Xie, Zhen Zhang, Zhuoqi Zeng, Amr Alanwar

item.title: Safe Performance-aware Online Input Design
item.description: arXiv:2611.12822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose an input design framework for the safe online excitation and identification of uncertain linear systems without requiring informative initial data. The objective is to actively excite the system and collect sufficiently informative input-output data while maintaining safe operation and satisfactory control performance. Achieving this objective is challenging due to the potential conflict between the excitation required for learning and the safety and performance requirements, particularly when limited prior knowledge of the system is available. Inspired by the dual control principle, the proposed scheme balances exploitation for control performance with exploration for model improvement. A Bayesian learning approach is employed to update the model uncertainty online, starting from a conservative initial uncertainty set. As informative data are collected, the uncertainty set contracts, enabling progressively less conservative operation. To reduce the online computational burden, the resulting program is reformulated into a computationally tractable form. Furthermore, an online ellipsoidal terminal set with non-increasing conservatism is designed to guarantee the recursive feasibility of the proposed scheme. Numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, particularly in terms of uncertainty reduction and control performance.
item.dc:creator: Diyou Liu, Mohammad Khosravi

item.title: Distributed Global Pose Synchronization for Heterogeneous Multiple Rigid Body Systems on SE(3)
item.description: arXiv:2611.12851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of global pose synchronization for heterogeneous multiple rigid-body systems evolving on the matrix Lie group $\SE(3)$. We first construct a new potential function on $\SE(3) \times \mathbb{R}$ with a generalized non-diagonal weighting matrix, together with a set of switching variables governed by continuous-discrete hybrid dynamics. Based on this new potential function and these switching variables, we propose a distributed hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative pose on $\SE(3)$ and group velocity measurements, endowed with global asymptotic stability guarantees. We then further propose a distributed velocity-free hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative and absolute pose measurements, without requiring group velocity measurements, while preserving global asymptotic stability. Numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed distributed hybrid control schemes.
item.dc:creator: Fengyu Lin, Miaomiao Wang, Housheng Su, Zhigang Zeng, Abdelhamid Tayebi

item.title: Continuous-Time Constrained Linear Quadratic Regulator for Switched Linear Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.12823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Switched systems, characterized by a family of subsystems governed by a switching rule, widely apply to complex real-world scenarios. However, their inherent switching dynamics pose significant challenges in phase analysis and control design. To address these challenges, we propose a framework for solving the Continuous-Time Constrained Linear Quadratic Regulator (CT-CLQR) problem for switched linear systems. Our approach partitions the time horizon into a finite number of intervals, each associated with a specific system mode. The duration of these intervals is parameterized by the switching instants, enabling a reformulation of the problem. We indirectly optimize the switching sequence by fixing the switching sequence and optimizing the interval durations. We derive analytical expressions for the cost function and its gradient, which are critical for efficient optimization. Unlike state-of-the-art methods that impose equality constraints on state evolution, our approach inherently considers the state evolution in the cost function. This not only simplifies the problem formulation but also reduces computational overhead by precomputing shared terms offline, enhancing efficiency during online operations. The proposed method significantly advances existing techniques, offering improved computational efficiency and flexibility. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through comprehensive numerical examples, showcasing its potential for practical applications.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Gori, Michele Pierallini, Franco Angelini, Manolo Garabini

item.title: Fresh Enough to Decide: Age of Intelligence for Cost-Aware Model Synchronization in Dynamic IoT Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.09935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resource-constrained IoT devices cache learned models for real-time decisions, but frequent updates incur substantial bandwidth, energy, and service overhead.
